variants.note: The family kit's own note names Pueblo Revival as the single deliberate exception to the family's forbidding of additive-vernacular composition. This style's own proportional_system states it directly: symmetry is 'additive-vernacular', and 'the absence of any framing module means proportion is judged as sculptural mass rather than as composition.'
Inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival; a hard-constraint violation here -- c01: 'any pitched roof visible from a principal elevation voids the style.'

roof_form.rule: Roof must be flat or near-flat, concealed behind an irregular parapet 18-30 in above the roof deck. Any pitched roof visible from a principal elevation voids the style (c01, hard).

roof_pitch_rise_per_12.note: Own text states the maximum as 1/4 in per foot of run, expressed here as an equivalent rise-per-12 value; effectively flat.

roof_pitch.rule: Maximum 1/4 in per foot to internal or canale drainage -- flat or near-flat (c01, hard).

variants.note: Inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival; this style has no eave of any kind -- c03: 'No eave, fascia, gutter, downspout, corner bead line, or applied trim may appear on the exterior.'

eave_condition.rule: No eave anywhere on the exterior; the flat roof deck is concealed entirely behind the parapet (c03, hard).

gable_treatment.note: The roof is flat behind a parapet; there is no gable end to treat (c01).

dormer.note: The roof is flat and concealed behind a parapet; a dormer has no roof slope to sit in (c01).

variants.note: Inherited from British Picturesque; contradicts the style's own governing description that 'the whole thing is one continuous rounded surface' with no dramatic vertical incident.

chimney.rule: Where a chimney is expressed at all it is a low, rounded, stuccoed stack consistent with the wall it rises from -- not a tall, deliberately conspicuous silhouette accent. Editorial inference from the style's own governing description; not a directly sourced chimney specification.

variants.note: massing_affinities: 'massed-picturesque' canonical -- 'the stepped, terraced accumulation of flat-roofed blocks at differing heights is the whole formal idea.'
massing_affinities: courtyard-u common -- 'the historically correct New Mexican domestic plan and the strongest residential option.'
Inherited from Mission Revival; too simple for this style's own defining stepped, terraced massing.
massing_affinities names this explicitly: 'a symmetrical double-pile block with a centred entrance is fundamentally alien to the type.'

wing_strategy.rule: Stepped, terraced massing of blocks at differing heights, set back from one another to recall the multi-storey Puebloan roomblock -- the whole formal idea, not a simple single block.

variants.note: diagnostic_tells: 'the revival often achieves the look in 2 in. of stucco over frame' -- the ordinary case.
The genuinely authentic material, but rare in revival work; distinguished_from names 18-36 in adobe as belonging to the original, not the revival.

construction_type.rule: Thick earth-toned stucco over wood frame, concrete block, or (rarely, and most authentically) adobe; walls read as continuous rounded mass with corners and arrises radiused not less than 3 in and a visible outward batter of 1 in 24 to 1 in 40 over the lower 3-6 ft.

variants.note: Inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival; this style's own colour is more specifically earth-toned -- 'the colour of the ground it stands on' -- rather than SCR's off-white-leaning range.

primary_cladding.rule: Thick earth-toned stucco, one continuous rounded surface with no eave, fascia, or applied trim to interrupt it.

foundation_expression.note: No masonry base or material change at grade -- the wall batters continuously into the ground at 1 in 24 to 1 in 40 over the lower 3-6 ft (typical_ratios), the same stucco surface throughout. Overrides the rock-faced stone base inherited from Shingle Style.

reveal_frame.rule: Wall thickness must be expressed with a minimum 10 in reveal at all openings, jambs and heads returned in stucco, corners and parapet arrises radiused not less than 3 in (c03, hard). Overrides the 6-12 in reveal inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival with this style's own, larger, hard-constraint minimum.

cornice.note: No cornice, fascia, or applied trim of any kind may appear on the exterior (c03, hard) -- overrides the plain-boxed cornice inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival.

variants.note: Inherited from Mission Revival; distinguished_from names this directly: Mission Revival 'has a pitched tile roof and a curvilinear shaped parapet on smooth machine-flat stucco. Pueblo Revival has a flat roof, an irregular parapet, rounded wall surfaces, and vigas.' The undulation here comes from hand-formed construction, not from a designed decorative curve.

parapet.rule: Parapet 18-30 in above the roof deck, its top line varying by at least 4 in over its length -- a dead-straight parapet indicates a Territorial or commercial building, not this style (c01, hard; diagnostic_tells).

variants.note: Inherited from Georgian Colonial American; this style's own drainage method is named directly in defining_characteristics: 'flat roof drained through projecting canales behind an irregular, gently undulating parapet.'

rainwater.rule: The flat roof drains through projecting canales (wood or metal spouts) piercing the parapet, or internally -- never a gutter and downspout, which c03 forbids outright.

variants.note: Inherited from Mission Revival; this style's own colour is explicitly earth-toned -- 'the colour of the ground it stands on... almost white at noon and burnt orange at five o'clock' -- not Mission Revival's pale/white body.

color_strategy.rule: Earth-toned stucco matching the local ground colour, reversing the pale-uniform-stucco canonical for Mission Revival.

overall_width_to_height.note: Own typical_ratios states 'openings 1:1.2 to 1:1.6' (height:width); expressed here as width:height = 0.625-0.833 -- more square than Mission Revival's own 0.45-0.625, and small relative to wall (solid-to-void 8:1 or greater).

window_proportion.rule: Openings 1:1.2 to 1:1.6, solid-to-void ratio 8:1 or greater on principal elevations -- small, deeply recessed, favouring wall.

window_surround_wood.rule: No applied wood casing anywhere; the opening's expression is the deeply returned stucco jamb (minimum 10 in reveal) and a heavy timber lintel at the head -- not, as in Spanish Colonial Revival, an arch.

window_grouping_rule.rule: Additive and irregular: openings are placed by internal need, do not align between storeys, and are separated by broad blank wall (bay_rhythm). Overrides the grouped A-BBB-A arched rhythm inherited from Richardsonian Romanesque, which presumes a compositional order this style does not have.

shutter.note: No applied trim of any kind on the exterior (c03, hard) -- overrides the raised-panel shutter pair inherited from Georgian Colonial American.

special_window.note: No decorative special window shape -- the quatrefoil window inherited from Mission Revival is that style's own signature, not this one's. Openings here are uniformly small, deeply recessed, and rectangular.

variants.note: Inherited from Spanish Colonial Revival, whose own c03 requires an elaborate carved entrance surround. distinguished_from states the opposite directly: Pueblo Revival 'has flat roofs, no tile, no worked ornament, and substitutes timber and earth for iron and glaze.'

door_surround.rule: No ornament at the entrance -- a deeply recessed opening with a heavy timber lintel, the same as any other opening in the wall, not a decorated frontispiece.

transom_sidelight.note: No applied trim on the exterior (c03) and no worked ornament at the entrance (distinguished_from vs. spanish-colonial-revival); a classical rectangular transom-and-sidelight assembly does not belong to this style's plain recessed openings. Editorial inference -- the style's own text does not address the entrance transom directly.

variants.note: Where the placita/courtyard-u plan is used (massing_affinities: common).

garage_strategy.rule: The car is housed in the lowest, plainest of the stepped terraced blocks the style's own massing is built from, or -- where a placita plan is used -- tucked behind the courtyard wall out of the principal elevation. No historical precedent exists for this element; this is an editorial extension of the style's own additive, stepped-block massing logic.

porch_type.rule: A portal -- a post-and-corbel covered porch with peeled log posts and carved corbels -- on at least one principal elevation (defining_characteristics). Where a gallery-house or portal fronts a linear range it is the standard Santa Fe street condition (massing_affinities).

porch_support.rule: Portal posts 8-10 in square or round at 7-9 ft on centre, with corbels 30-42 in long (typical_ratios) -- peeled log, not a classical or Craftsman post.

porch_rail.rule: The portal is typically open between posts, with no applied rail -- consistent with the style's own blanket prohibition on applied trim (c03). Editorial inference; the style's own text does not address a porch rail directly.
